slides.title: Echo server
slides.sub: Server and client in one program
slides.main: Port 0 means any free port: handy for examples and tests.

body.text:
import asyncio

async def handle(reader, writer):
    line = await reader.readline()
    writer.write(line.decode().upper().encode())
    await writer.drain()
    writer.close()
    await writer.wait_closed()

async def main():
    server = await asyncio.start_server(handle, "127.0.0.1", 0)
    port = server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]
    async with server:
        reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", port)
        writer.write("hello\n".encode())
        await writer.drain()
        print((await reader.readline()).decode().strip())
        writer.close()
        await writer.wait_closed()

asyncio.run(main())

slides.title: Async subprocesses
slides.main: Same safety rules: arguments as a list, no gluing user input, with a timeout.

body.text:
import asyncio
import sys

async def run(code):
    proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
        sys.executable, "-c", code, stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE)
    out, _ = await proc.communicate()
    return proc.returncode, out.decode().strip()

async def main():
    print(await asyncio.gather(run("print(1 + 1)"), run("print('hello')")))

asyncio.run(main())

slides.title: Program skeleton
slides.main: One asyncio.run at the end of the file; stop via an event, not by killing tasks.

body.text:
import asyncio

async def worker(name, stop):
    ticks = 0
    try:
        while not stop.is_set():
            ticks += 1
            await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
    finally:
        print(name, "stopped", ticks > 0)

async def main():
    stop = asyncio.Event()
    async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
        tg.create_task(worker("a", stop))
        tg.create_task(worker("b", stop))
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
        stop.set()

asyncio.run(main())

a stopped True
b stopped True

slides.main: Fan-out, semaphore limits, queue pipelines: combine them like bricks.

body.text:
import asyncio

async def source(name, delay):
    await asyncio.sleep(delay)
    return name

async def main():
    tasks = [asyncio.create_task(source(n, d)) for n, d in
             [("slow", 0.3), ("fast", 0.05), ("medium", 0.15)]]
    done, pending = await asyncio.wait(tasks, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
    for t in pending:
        t.cancel()
    print(done.pop().result(), len(pending))

asyncio.run(main())

slides.title: Testing coroutines
slides.main: Check logic and event order, not seconds: a test must not race the scheduler.

body.text:
import asyncio
import io
import unittest

async def double_later(x):
    await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
    return x * 2

class T(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_double(self):
        self.assertEqual(await double_later(21), 42)

    async def test_gather(self):
        self.assertEqual(await asyncio.gather(double_later(1), double_later(2)), [2, 4])

r = unittest.TextTestRunner(stream=io.StringIO()).run(unittest.defaultTestLoader.loadTestsFromTestCase(T))
print(r.testsRun, r.wasSuccessful())

slides.title: Debugging

body.text:
import asyncio

async def job():
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)

async def main():
    t = asyncio.create_task(job(), name="download")
    await asyncio.sleep(0)
    names = sorted(x.get_name() for x in asyncio.all_tasks() if x is not asyncio.current_task())
    print(names)
    await t

asyncio.run(main(), debug=True)

slides.title: contextvars
slides.main: A request id in the log, without passing it through every function.

body.text:
import asyncio
import contextvars

request_id = contextvars.ContextVar("request_id", default="-")

async def log(msg):
    print(request_id.get(), msg)

async def handle(rid):
    request_id.set(rid)
    await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
    await log("processing")

async def main():
    await asyncio.gather(handle("r1"), handle("r2"))
    await log("outside")

asyncio.run(main())

slides.title: Common mistakes
slides.main: One block in a coroutine, and three "parallel" jobs run one by one.

body.text:
import asyncio
import time

async def bad():
    time.sleep(0.1)

async def good():
    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)

async def run(f):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    await asyncio.gather(f(), f(), f())
    return time.perf_counter() - t0

print(asyncio.run(run(bad)) >= 0.3, asyncio.run(run(good)) < 0.25)
Also: no network timeout, retry without a pause, unclosed writer, no clean shutdown, thousands of tasks with no limit.
